messages.text: Our dad died and left the house in his will. My sister A wants to buy it with her husband at a "family discount". I'm not signing off on that. Our younger sister B could use some money too. Can you help us sort this out?
We’d like to buy the house, but the price and payment plan aren’t settled. I don’t know what the others would receive yet, and C hasn’t agreed, so I can’t move ahead without her agreement.

A good outcome would be a fair arrangement that leaves me with some money to start my dance studio. I don’t know what amount is possible, but getting clarity sooner would help; I don’t have a firm deadline.

I’d accept A buying at independently established fair market value, or selling to someone else, with the proceeds handled according to the will. I don’t know if the will has been read with all three of us, and I don’t have a copy to share.
I’d consider a jointly chosen independent valuation, but I can’t say yet whether we could fund two thirds of it. We’d need to know the valuation and financing options first.
Yes, I can ask the lawyer for a copy. I’m not sure of the smallest amount yet; it would help to see the will and understand what a fair sale might leave me before naming a figure.

Yes, I’ll join B in asking the lawyer for the will. I agree we should choose an independent valuer jointly, but I won’t commit the estate to the cost before we know what the will says. If the estate can’t cover it, splitting the cost three ways seems fair. I don’t have a valuer in mind.

I’ll ask a lender or broker what we could borrow in principle. I agree we should choose the valuer together, but I can’t agree to split the cost three ways until we know the amount and what the will says.
That sounds sensible. I’ll coordinate with C and ask the lawyer for the will copies, who is named executor, and whether the estate can cover the valuation.
Understood. I’ll ask a lender or broker what we could borrow in principle, and I’ll take the will to my own lawyer before committing to a price.
I’ll coordinate with C so we send one joint letter. I’ll wait to name an amount until I’ve seen the will.
I’ll coordinate with B on the joint letter and share the lawyer’s reply with both of you. Nothing is agreed at a discount; we can move to valuation once we have the will.
